links.comparator_used: Original, unrevised validated spine PROMs before ChatGPT 4.0 revision
links.outcome: Readability of validated spine patient-reported outcome measures and preservation of validated content
links.effect: Eighteen of nineteen linguistic parameters improved significantly (p < .05); word count decreased by 18%; all readability indices improved (p < .001); about 7 of 9 grade-level metrics achieved NIH/AMA sixth-grade readability compliance following revision. However, 59.7% of PROMs contained at least one content-related error; alteration of validated response scales (23%), omission or simplification of recall timeframes (18%), and consolidation of multiple items into single prompts (16%).
links.tradeoff: Frequent content-related errors affecting validated instrument structure: 59.7% of PROMs had at least one content-related error, including altered response scales, omitted or simplified recall timeframes, and consolidated items.
links.quote: ChatGPT 4.0 substantially improved the readability of validated spine PROMs but frequently introduced structural modifications affecting validated content.

links.comparator_used: Original PROMs before revision (no comparison against a prompt without reading-level instruction)
links.outcome: Readability of PROMs after ChatGPT revision with a standardized prompt instructing a sixth-grade reading level
links.effect: 7 of 9 grade-level metrics achieved NIH/AMA sixth-grade compliance after revision; all readability indices improved (p < .001)
links.tradeoff: 59.7% of revised PROMs had at least one content-related error, including altered response scales (23%) and omitted recall timeframes (18%)
links.quote: About 7 of 9 grade-level metrics achieved NIH/AMA sixth-grade readability compliance following revision.

design_hint: reading-level constraint in prompt with content fidelity check
